title: The Last Hollow Revisited
premise: Xanthe Thackeray, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Vessia, has spent years keeping the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled memories, borrowed luck, doors to nowhere. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, she learns her guild's masters engineered both catastrophes to sever their country from history and seize divinity for themselves. Hunted by former comrades and guided by a ragtag found family of debtors and defectors, Xanthe must locate the Last Hollow—the original door out of a country that is being unwritten—and decide whether loyalty to her oath or the truth of what her god actually asked of her matters more. In the end she reopens the door not to escape but to let the stolen stars back in, sacrificing her guild-name and her god's protection, and walks out into an ordinary world with her chosen family intact.
about_author: Juniper Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that no longer exist. They write fantasy about paperwork, gods, and the people who fall through the cracks between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A quiet night balancing the Hollow Guild's accounts: a jar of someone's childhood, a week of good weather sold twice. Through her careful bookkeeping we meet the guild's strange economy and her own invisible place in it. Emotional beat: contentment built on willful blindness.

chapters.title: Oath and Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Flashback woven into present: how she swore herself to Vessia as a starving child soldier, and how the god went silent seven years ago. Her handler, Magister Corvel, tests her loyalty with a small cruelty. Emotional beat: grief disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge: Xanthe on the guildhouse roof, ferryman Odji on the river, apprentice Wren in the archives—all witness the sky going black and the border wards shattering like glass. Panic spreads; the guild locks its doors. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Entries Written in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Auditing the ledgers after the catastrophe, she finds pages she never recorded—transactions dating back decades, signed in her own name, describing the ward-fall as a planned purchase. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of her identity.

chapters.title: Debtors at the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The city frays; those who owe the guild—or are owed—flood the guildhouse. Xanthe quietly tears up debts, her first open rebellion. She gathers her unlikely circle: Odji, Wren, and disgraced ward-smith Brannoc. Emotional beat: first sparks of found family.

chapters.title: What Corvel Bought
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. He reveals the wards didn't fail—they were sold, and the buyer used guild coin. Corvel and the inner circle intend to seal the country off from the cosmos entirely and crown themselves new gods in the dark. Emotional beat: betrayal made concrete.

chapters.title: The Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Odji's POV. The group travels toward the old capital and finds maps refusing to hold: roads loop, villages remember different names, travelers arrive before they leave. The country is being unwritten from its edges inward. Emotional beat: vertigo and mounting urgency.

chapters.title: A Chapel with No God In It
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sheltering in a ruined chapel of Vessia, Xanthe rages at her silent god—and finds a fresco showing Vessia not as a giver of power but a jailer of doors. Emotional beat: faith cracking into dangerous questions.

chapters.title: The Guild Comes Collecting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Enforcers led by Xanthe's old sword-sister Ivetta catch up. A brutal skirmish on a bridge that exists in two places at once; the group escapes only because Odji knows the river's older name. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized against them.

chapters.title: Ivetta's Terms
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. Captured briefly by her former comrades' logic, Ivetta offers Xanthe amnesty if she surrenders the ledgers—the guild needs them to complete the sealing. Xanthe refuses. Emotional beat: two kinds of loyalty colliding without villains.

chapters.title: Borrowed Luck Runs Out
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. A desperate crossing of the Sablefen using hoarded guild-luck, which burns out mid-marsh. Brannoc nearly drowns saving Wren; the group realizes they've spent their last advantages. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged in cost.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Capital
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They infiltrate the drowned archive where the original contracts are kept and learn the truth: Vessia wasn't silent—she was devoured, her divinity split among the guild's inner circle. Emotional beat: horror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Corvel Ascendant
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. In the half-dark capital, Corvel begins his apotheosis, rewriting citizens' memories into worship. He offers Xanthe a place at his right hand—as he once offered her mentor. Emotional beat: seduction of power, refused at real price.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The archive reveals the Last Hollow's location—and its toll: it opens only for someone who surrenders every name the guild ever gave them, including 'Xanthe Thackeray.' The group argues over whether she should pay it. Emotional beat: love arguing against sacrifice.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Odji's POV. A night of rest before the end: shared stories, mended gear, Wren teaching Brannoc letters, Odji giving Xanthe a river-charm 'for whoever you turn out to be.' Emotional beat: tenderness as armor.

chapters.title: Storm of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The final unmaking begins; the capital's streets erase themselves while Corvel's ascension peaks. The group fights through collapsing geography to reach the Hollow's mountain door, losing supplies, certainty, and time. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Sister Against Sister
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Ivetta blocks the door—not from malice but because she believes sealed safety beats open ruin. A duel that is also an argument; Xanthe wins by refusing to kill, breaking Ivetta's certainty instead. Emotional beat: mercy as victory.

chapters.title: The Last Hollow
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the threshold, Xanthe speaks her renunciation—every guild-name, every oath—discovering in the process Vessia's final message hidden in her own ledger-hand: the god meant the silence as a test of who would open the door. Emotional beat: revelation and release.

chapters.title: Let There Be Stars
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe throws open the Hollow as Corvel arrives in half-made godhood; the stolen stars pour back through the door, burning away his borrowed divinity. The country snaps back into existence around them. Emotional beat: catastrophic, luminous reversal.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The guild dissolves; debts become moot, enforcers scatter, Ivetta walks away carrying the true ledgers to be read aloud publicly. The survivors reckon with what was lost and what was never theirs to keep. Emotional beat: exhausted reckoning.

chapters.title: A Woman With No Guild-Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Stripped of her names, Xanthe chooses a plain one and takes work that is honestly ordinary. Corvel survives, mortal and diminished, awaiting judgment rather than apotheosis. Emotional beat: humility as hard-won peace.

chapters.title: Doors We Leave Open
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating brief POVs. One year later: Odji's ferry runs under real stars, Wren teaches in a rebuilt archive, Brannoc wards doors that open freely. Xanthe keeps a small shop of possible things—and leaves the back door unlocked. Emotional beat: belonging, freely chosen.
